The FOMC statement remains constructive on growth and employment and notes modest further progress on inflation, while keeping rates steady and emphasizing data dependence. However, the latest SLOOS indicates tighter credit supply and softer demand across key lending categories: banks tightened standards and terms for C&I and consumer loans (including credit cards and autos), widened spreads and raised credit score requirements, reported weaker loan demand, and further tightened CRE lending (lower LTVs, higher DSCRs, shorter interest-only periods, narrower market areas) amid concerns about rents, vacancies, and property prices. These credit headwinds, layered onto higher-for-longer rates, point to a more cautious backdrop for households and businesses than the statement alone implies. Netting solid current activity against tighter bank lending, the tone shifts from moderately positive to cautiously positive.
